t.2.62.1: Having heard those words of theirs, Vasiṣṭha replied with this speech to all the groups of friends and ministers and to those brāhmaṇas.
t.2.62.2: For Bharata lives happily in the house of his maternal uncle, in the city of Rājagṛha, together with his brother Śatrughna.
t.2.62.3: Therefore let swift messengers go quickly on speedy horses to bring back the two heroic brothers. What are we waiting for?
t.2.62.4: Then they all spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha: "Let them go." Having heard those words of theirs, Vasiṣṭha spoke these words.
t.2.62.5: Come, Siddhārtha, Vijaya, Jayanta, Aśoka and Nandana! Let what must be done be heard; I tell it to all of you.
t.2.62.6: Having gone swiftly to the city of Rājagṛha on swift-paced horses, you must cast off your grief and tell Bharata this at my command.
t.2.62.7: The family priest and all the ministers send you their wishes for your welfare. Set out in haste, for there is urgent business that must be done by you.
t.2.62.8: When you have gone there, you must not tell him that Rāma has been exiled, nor that his father is dead, nor of this ruin of the Rāghavas.
t.2.62.9: "Take silken garments and excellent ornaments for the king and for Bharata, and go quickly." Given leave by Vasiṣṭha, the messengers set out in great haste.
t.2.62.10: Having crossed the Gaṅgā at Hastinapura, they went on facing west, and reaching the land of the Pāñcālas, they passed through the middle of Kurujāṅgala.
t.2.62.11: They swiftly crossed the Śaradaṇḍā, a divine river with clear waters, frequented by many kinds of birds and crowded with people.
t.2.62.12: Reaching the divine Nikūla tree, through which prayers come true, and approaching that tree worthy of reverence, they entered the city of Kuliṅgā.
t.2.62.14: Those messengers, their mounts exhausted, travelling by a long road, quickly and directly reached Girivraja, the finest of cities.
t.2.62.13: Then, having reached Abhikāla and moved on from Tejobhibhavana, they went through the midst of the Vāhlīkas to Mount Sudāman, gazing upon the footprint of Viṣṇu, the Vipāśā, and the Śālmalī as well.
t.2.62.15: To do what was dear to their master, to protect the family, and to secure the continuity of their master's lineage, the messengers pressed on in haste without flagging, and they reached that very city at night.
